short: the code new runs on a freshly zeroed object. same name as the class, no return type, never inherited.
a bare { } block in a class body. javac pastes it into every constructor that calls super(...).
a static { } block. runs once, when the class is initialized, collected with static field initializers into <clinit>.
the access you get with no modifier: visible to the same package, nobody else.
package-private plus subclasses in other packages, which may only use it through their own type.
a class's real name, package included: java.util.ArrayList. imports are just shorthand for it.
a subclass replacing an inherited method with the same signature. the object's class picks which runs, at runtime.
a subclass field with the same name as a parent's. both exist in the object; the variable's declared type picks one.
an interface method with a body. implementers get it unless they override it. java 8.
inheriting the same method from two places. java's rules: class wins, then the more specific interface, else you must override.
a final class with a fixed set of singleton instances, one per constant, created at class init.
the hidden field an inner class uses to reach the outer object that created it. a classic memory leak.
copying a mutable argument or return value so callers can't change your object's state behind its back.
a subclass breaking when its superclass changes, because overriding couples it to the parent's implementation.
holding an object in a field and forwarding calls to it, instead of extending its class.
